# Template: Governance Bootstrap Notice (appended to .governance/GOVERNANCE_INDEX.md)

## Purpose

First-session notice that AI-DWG appends to `.governance/GOVERNANCE_INDEX.md` after provisioning the companion engines (AI-GCE / AI-TGE). It tells the dev team how to activate governance and test enforcement in this workspace.

**Generated by:** `mapping/companion-bootstrap.md` (Step 4)
**Ownership:** `generated` (DWG places it once; GCE/TGE may extend it on first activation)
**Condition:** Config Gate Q3 ≠ No AND the target GOVERNANCE_INDEX.md does not already contain the companion bootstrap marker.

---

## Template Content

The following block is appended to `.governance/GOVERNANCE_INDEX.md`, wrapped in markers so it can be replaced on re-provision:

```markdown
<!-- COMPANION-BOOTSTRAP:start -->
## Governance Engines — Ready to Activate

AI-DWG has provisioned the following governance engines into this workspace:

| Engine | Location | Activation Key | Purpose |
|--------|----------|:--------------:|---------|
| AI-GCE | `.governance/engine/ai-gce/` | `_GCE_` | Compliance enforcement — hooks, rules, agents, drift detection |
| AI-TGE | `.governance/engine/ai-tge/` | `_TGE_` | Test governance — strategy, register, coverage, quality dashboard |

### How to Activate

1. **Start a new AI chat session** in this workspace (recommended: one package per session).
2. Type **`_GCE_`** to activate AI-GCE. It will read the workspace steering (`rules/`) and derive a tailored compliance enforcement layer (hooks, agents, rules) specific to this project.
3. Once governance is running, type **`_TGE_`** to activate AI-TGE. It will read the architecture + backlog and derive a test strategy, register, and coverage tracking.

> **Order matters:** activate GCE first (it establishes the enforcement framework), then TGE (it builds on the governance structure).

### What Happens on Activation

- The engine reads `rules/` + `.governance/workspace-manifest.yaml` to understand the workspace
- It derives its artifacts into `.governance/` (rules, hooks, agents, test artifacts)
- It renders per-platform wiring for your tool(s): {platformTargets}
- Nothing is auto-enforced until you activate — this is human-in-the-loop

### Platform Enforcement Tiers

| Your Tool | What You Get |
|-----------|--------------|
| Kiro | Full: native auto-firing hooks + CI/CD gates + advisory rules |
| Cursor / Claude Code / Amazon Q / Cline | CI/CD gates + advisory rules (no auto-firing hooks) |
| Codex / Generic | CI/CD gates (if git) + advisory rules |

See `PLATFORM_NOTES.md` (generated alongside workspace) for details.

### Not Ready Yet?

No action required. The engines are dormant until you activate them. Your workspace works without governance enforcement — it's an opt-in upgrade.
<!-- COMPANION-BOOTSTRAP:end -->
```

---

## Generation Rules

1. **Marker-guarded.** The block is wrapped in `<!-- COMPANION-BOOTSTRAP:start/end -->` so DWG can replace it on re-provision without duplicating.
2. **Respect Q3 selection.** If only GCE provisioned (Q3 = GCE-only), omit the AI-TGE row from the table and adjust the narrative. Vice versa for TGE-only.
3. **Substitute `{platformTargets}`.** Replace with the actual list from Config Gate Q2.
4. **Idempotent.** If the marker block already exists in GOVERNANCE_INDEX.md, replace its content (don't append a second copy).
5. **Do NOT populate the rest of GOVERNANCE_INDEX.md.** GCE owns the full index; DWG only appends this bootstrap section. If GOVERNANCE_INDEX.md doesn't exist yet, create a minimal shell:
   ```markdown
   <!-- DWG-BASELINE: v{N} | {projectId} | {timestamp} -->
   # Governance Index

   > This workspace uses AI-GCE + AI-TGE for governance enforcement. The sections below are populated on first activation.

   {bootstrap notice block}
   ```
